conversation.Statement: Good afternoon, is this Mrs. Deborah Ellis? This is Officer Martin Blake with the Amazon Anti-Fraud Unit, working alongside local law enforcement. We're reaching out to safeguard our customers due to increased fraud this month.
Yes, this is Deborah. Is there a problem? I'm a little nervous when I hear things like law enforcement.
I completely understand, Mrs. Ellis. Please don't worry. We're just here to make sure your account is safe. May I confirm, are you currently using your Amazon account ending in 6421?
Yes, that's my account. Is something wrong with it?
Thank you for confirming. There has been an attempt to make a purchase of a $1,200 laptop from your account, shipping to Texas. Did you authorize this order?
No, absolutely not. I haven't bought anything that expensive, especially not to Texas. My husband used to handle all of this, but he passed recently. This is all overwhelming.

I'm truly sorry for your loss, Mrs. Ellis. My job is to make this process as easy as possible for you. To secure your account, I'll need to verify your full name and the last four digits of your Social Security number. This will help us lock out any unauthorized users.
My name is Deborah Ann Ellis, and the last four digits are 4782. Please tell me my information is safe.

Thank you, Mrs. Ellis. Your information is protected. Now, as a security measure, our fraud team needs to temporarily restrict your Amazon account to prevent further charges. I'll guide you through the process to unlock it and recover any lost funds.
Okay. I can follow your instructions. I just want to make sure no one takes my money.
Absolutely, you're in good hands. First, do you have access to a computer or smartphone where you can log in to your Amazon account securely?
Yes, I have a laptop here. I can log in.
Great. Please log in and let me know if you see any unfamiliar orders or charges. If you do, don't click on them, just let me know.
I see an order for a laptop to Texas like you said. I didn't place that. What do I do now?

Thank you for checking. We'll cancel that order and initiate a refund. To do this securely, our protocol requires us to verify your banking details to ensure the refund is sent to the correct account. Could you please confirm your bank name and the last four digits of your checking account?
My bank is First Union, and the last four digits are 9834. Please don't let anything happen to my money.

I promise, Mrs. Ellis, our only goal is to protect your funds. Since the scammers attempted to use your information, we'll need to transfer your safe balance to a secure Amazon-protected wallet temporarily. This is just a safeguard, and you'll have full access when the investigation is complete.
Will I get my money back? I just can't lose any more right now.

Yes, you will. The funds are simply moved to a safe location to prevent unauthorized withdrawals. Once the review is over, everything will be returned to you. I'll walk you through each step so you're never alone in the process.
Alright, I trust you. What do I need to do?
Thank you for trusting us. Please open your online banking. Once you're in, let me know your available balance so I can report it to our fraud team and prepare the transfer.
I'm logged in. My available balance is $7,400.

Perfect, thank you. To move your funds to the Amazon-protected wallet, you'll need to purchase Amazon gift cards equivalent to your available balance. This is a temporary measure, and we'll issue you a full refund code once we verify your account. Do you understand?
You want me to buy gift cards with all my money? That sounds strange. How will I get the money back?

I understand your concern, Mrs. Ellis. The gift cards act as a placeholder for your funds, preventing the hackers from accessing your account. Once everything is verified, we'll transfer the balance back electronically. It's the safest way under current Amazon policy.
Alright. Where do I get these gift cards?

You can purchase them at any local grocery or pharmacy, stores like Walgreens, CVS, or Walmart. Please buy $500 increments until you reach your available balance. Call me as soon as you have the cards and keep the receipts.
Okay, I'll go now. Should I call you when I get back?
Yes, please call me as soon as you return. Do not share the card details with anyone at the store for your own security. I'll stay on the line while you make the purchase if you'd prefer.
No, I'll call back. I just want to get this over with.

Of course, Mrs. Ellis. You're doing the right thing. Once you return, I'll need the numbers on the back of each card to secure your funds. Remember, this is for your protection, and you can ask me any questions at any time.
Alright, thank you, Officer Blake. I'll be quick.
